findings.subjectClaim: Both earlier turn subjects remain frozen at their cited digests, and CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 has been landed.
findings.liveFact: Neither digest exists anywhere in the repository. A sha256 sweep of every file under the working tree excluding .git and node_modules returns no match for 0df0ab46db65d4360a5fc7f071c434275a074a49b127aa639d46579375a0db39 and no match for b20660b5007793c8d5793edca3ac21bfdf3f7a9482617e9bbfc63a9d0547d7ed. The only path that ever held those bytes, docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.draft.md, now measures 7fc4e738ce0db700349cc4d94f7a83404c5789c418f016371e4a1b144411437d at 15511 bytes and 136 lines; each turn was written in place over its predecessor. The file is untracked, so git holds no blob of either state either: git ls-files --error-unmatch on that path returns 'did not match any file(s) known to git'. The two digests are correct recitations of what the turn-1 and turn-2 review prompts pinned as the then-expected subject, and of subjectMeasuredSha256 in the two frozen Claude reviews, but 'remains frozen' is a present-tense custody assertion and no bytes back it. Every prior multi-turn round in the register kept the earlier turn retrievable at a distinct path, which is why the same sentence was true there: D-320 cites frozen turn-1 subject coordinator-decisions.D-320.draft.md alongside turn-2 subject coordinator-decisions.D-320.turn2.draft.md, and D-341 and D-342 do the same. D-353 has no such second path.
findings.requiredCorrection: Land the custody half of CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 as that finding actually specified. Its requiredCorrection reads, verbatim from the frozen turn-2 review at f3cbc3cfbfe44bcbc942568940fb99ad449d7ef360ca7c1045adab3c3c14b7af: 'record turn-1 subject custody as it actually stands, naming the turn-1 digest 0df0ab46db65d4360a5fc7f071c434275a074a49b127aa639d46579375a0db39 and the fact that the turn-2 revision was written at the turn-1 path rather than claiming the turn-1 subject remains frozen.' Either restore the two earlier byte-states to distinct frozen paths and cite those paths, or replace both sentences with what is true: the turn-1 subject measured 0df0ab46 and the turn-2 subject measured b20660b5 when each was reviewed, each digest pinned by its own turn's review prompt and by subjectMeasuredSha256 in the corresponding frozen review, and each was overwritten in place at docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.draft.md rather than kept frozen. Invent no identifier while doing so.
findings.whyThisIsAMustFix: The entry names CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 as landed at line 7. It landed the turn-recitation half and inverted the custody half, asserting in the permanent record precisely what the finding required it not to assert. A decision that records a finding as landed while contradicting that finding's stated correction misreports its own adoption history, and the misreport is not recoverable from elsewhere once the earlier bytes are gone.
findings.whyNotCosmetic: This is not a wording preference. It is a false present-tense custody claim about two byte-states that no longer exist, made in the one paragraph whose whole function is to record how this decision was adopted. It is also the second half of a MUST-FIX the entry claims to have discharged, so leaving it stands the register's landing record on a statement its own frozen evidence refutes.

observations.note: The subject's Decision paragraph says 'Claude Stage A leftover-join.v32 of G21 returned 5 unlabeled observations strings; they travel as honesty work and this entry invents no identifier', while the Protocol paragraph says the v31 Stage A Claude review returned 5 labeled observation objects OBS-1 through OBS-5. Two different shapes for two adjacent versions invites a reading that one of them is wrong.

reviewSummary: The subject lands the turn-recitation demands cleanly. Protocol reads turn 3 of 3, MF-1 is named four times, CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 is named, Codex turn-2 MUST-FIX MF-1 is named as the same class, and the leftover-join.v31 Stage A Claude observations are now recited as 5 labeled objects OBS-1 through OBS-5 with members id and note, which is exactly what the frozen review carries. Stage A dual ACCEPT 0/0 on leftover-join.v32 of G21 holds: all thirty-four return-shape sub-claims across the two Stage A reviews measure correctly, the successor's status, binds, leftoverDesign and leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded all match, every predecessor landing claim from v29 through v31 holds, and every live-authority claim about HEAD, last heading, required-now 28, condition 2 at 5 of 32 and condition 4 MET reads correctly off the live register. Twenty of the twenty-two digests the entry cites recompute exactly. Three defects block consent, all of the same class: claims contradicted by the frozen bytes they describe. First, the entry declares CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 landed while asserting that the turn-1 and turn-2 subjects remain frozen; a repository-wide sha256 sweep finds neither byte-state anywhere, the draft is untracked so git holds no copy, and that finding's requiredCorrection had specifically demanded the entry record the in-place overwrite 'rather than claiming the turn-1 subject remains frozen'. Second, the Codex Stage B turn-1 return shape is recited as having no observationsNotFindings field, and the frozen review at the digest this entry itself cites carries that field as an empty list. Third, the Claude Stage B turn-2 observations are recited as uniformly carrying whyNotASeparateFinding, and only OBS-1 does; OBS-2, OBS-3 and OBS-4 carry whyNotAFinding. None of the three touches the recorded G21 lineage or the Stage A dual ACCEPT, and each has a narrow textual repair.
